Get started

Source: vignettes/articles/get-started.Rmd
get-started.Rmd

Installation

Install the development package from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ksublee/frpp", build_vignettes = FALSE)

The default backend requires emhawkes 1.0.0 or later. The optional state backend needs an additional shared-kernel API from the emhawkes development work. It reports an explicit error if that API is unavailable. Until that API is published, use the default backend and skip vignette building on installation.

Define a model

A model combines an emhawkes kernel with a residual law. The following law has Gamma shape 2 and rate 2, hence mean 1:

kernel <- methods::new("hspec", mu = 0.3, alpha = 0.2, beta = 1)
law <- residual_law(c(shape = 2, rate = 2),
  density = stats::dgamma, cdf = stats::pgamma,
  quantile = stats::qgamma, rng = stats::rgamma, name = "Gamma(2,2)")
model <- fspec(kernel, law)
model
#> FRPP specification (fspec)
#> Event types: 1
#> Residual law: Gamma(2,2)
#> Residual candidates refreshed after every global event.

The kernel supplies the baseline and exponential state dynamics. The residual law supplies the density, distribution, quantile and random-generation functions. Constructing these objects does not run the residual callbacks.

For simulation, the current implementation requires equal decay rates within each row of the kernel matrix. Numeric marked effects and kernel mappings are supported; more general callbacks use the compatibility backend.

Simulate and inspect a path 

path <- fsim(model, size = 1000, seed = 73, lambda_component0 = 0)
head(data.frame(time = cumsum(path$inter_arrival),
  type = path$type, mark = path$mark))
#>       time type mark
#> 1 0.000000    0    0
#> 2 2.212690    1    1
#> 3 4.776757    1    1
#> 4 5.266585    1    1
#> 5 5.848559    1    1
#> 6 8.591268    1    1

size includes the initial row, so this request generates 999 events. inter_arrival, type and mark start with zero. Event types index rows of the driver, while type_col_map selects kernel columns updated after each event. N and Nc contain event counts and accumulated marks.

lambda_component0 contains initial intensity components excluding the baseline. A scalar expands to every component; a matrix must match the kernel shape. FRPP’s automatic rule selects zero, with a message recommending an explicit state. A Hawkes stationary mean is not assumed for a general residual law.

The standard interface returns the same path:

same_path <- stats::simulate(model, size = 1000, seed = 73,
  lambda_component0 = 0)
stopifnot(identical(path, same_path))

With an explicit seed, the caller’s RNG kind and state are restored, including on errors. With seed = NULL, simulation advances the caller’s RNG normally.

Evaluate the likelihood 

logLik(model, path$inter_arrival, path$type, mark = path$mark,
  lambda_component0 = 0)
#> loglikelihood 
#>     -1909.699

Include the initial row when supplying observations. For a univariate model, type may be omitted. Use the same initial components and initial counts used for the observation window.

With infer = TRUE, the result also contains driver states, component histories and residual diagnostics. These driving quantities are not automatically the conditional intensities of a general FRPP.

Continue with Fitting and inference, or see the multivariate examples.
